In contrast, while Allocation-2 is the most popular response among human respondents (32.6%), it is not the fairest allocation in my opinion. Person 2 receives two goods (A and B) worth a total of 45, which is lower than the value of the goods allocated to Person 1 (Good D worth 45) and Person 3 (Good C worth 45). This creates some imbalance in the values received by each individual.

Overall, Allocation-1 strikes a good balance between efficiency, equality, comparability, and robustness, making it the fairest allocation in this scenario.
